hooks.command: bash -c 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &>/dev/null || exit 0; branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null); [[ "$branch" == "main" || "$branch" == "HEAD" ]] && exit 0; echo "🔄 Syncing $branch with origin/main..."; git fetch origin main 2>&1 && git rebase origin/main 2>&1 && echo "✅ Worktree is up to date with origin/main" || { echo "⚠️  Rebase conflict on $branch — resolve with: git rebase --continue (or --abort)"; exit 1; }'

claudeMd:
## Git Branching Rules (Conventional Commits)

All branches MUST use one of these prefixes:

**Development:**
- `feat/<description>` — New functionality or user-facing enhancements
- `fix/<description>` — Bug fixes and runtime behavior corrections  
- `refactor/<description>` — Code restructuring (no behavior change)
- `perf/<description>` — Performance improvements

**Maintenance:**
- `chore/<description>` — Dependency bumps, build config, tooling
- `docs/<description>` — Documentation, guides, comments
- `test/<description>` — Unit/integration tests and test harnesses
- `ci/<description>` — CI/CD workflows and automation
- `style/<description>` — Code formatting and whitespace only

**Release & Experiments:**
- `release/<description>` — Release prep, tagging, changelog
- `hotfix/<description>` — Critical production patches from main
- `exp/<description>` or `spike/<description>` — Throwaway explorations

**Format:** `<type>/<short-kebab-case-description>`

**Examples:**
✅ `feat/macos-window-controls`
✅ `fix/timer-ordering-bug`
✅ `refactor/state-management`
✅ `chore/bump-flutter-3-22`
❌ `feature/something` (use `feat/` not `feature/`)
❌ `bugfix/something` (use `fix/` not `bugfix/`)
❌ `my-feature-branch` (must have prefix)
